title: Narration and voice
purpose: Measures the delivery (coverage, words per minute, pauses, emphasis, processing) so a licensed or synthetic voice can reproduce it, without cloning or keeping the source voice.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: A1 spectrograms of 2-3 sentences, A4 silences, A6 RMS for emphasis; never save or splice the voice.
pitfalls: Guessing speaker identity, age or ethnicity; describe pitch register and delivery only
Calling a voice synthetic from quality alone
Computing wpm over the whole runtime instead of speech time

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.ms: {"value": n, "unit": "ms"} optionally with "min"/"max"; signed when an offset (negative = earlier)
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.text: one technique description, at most 300 characters, no copied content
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.timestamps: array of seconds from the start of the source
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F2: Burst sheet, 10 frames over 1 s: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 1 -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=10,scale=270:-2,tile=5x2" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/burst_T.jpg"
recipes.F3: Full-resolution crop (add ,scale=iw*2:-1:flags=lanczos to enlarge): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" "$WORK/crop_T.png"
recipes.A1: Spectrogram image (add highpass=f=3000, before showspectrumpic to isolate clicks and whooshes): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t D -i "$SRC" -lavfi "showspectrumpic=s=1200x600:legend=1" "$WORK/spec_T.png"
recipes.A3: Momentary loudness every 100 ms (LUFS): ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -af "ebur128=metadata=1,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.r128.M:file=$WORK/lufs_m.txt" -f null -
recipes.A5: Side (L-R) channel loudness, which removes centre-panned voice and leaves most stereo music: replace the A3 filter with "pan=mono|c0=0.5*c0-0.5*c1,ebur128=metadata=1,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.r128.M:file=$WORK/side_m.txt"; mid channel uses 0.5*c0+0.5*c1. Only meaningful for stereo sources.
recipes.A6: RMS level per 100 ms at 48 kHz: ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -af "aresample=48000,asetnsamples=n=4800,astats=metadata=1:reset=1,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level:file=$WORK/rms.txt" -f null -

questions.question: Is there narration, and what share of the runtime is covered by speech?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills narration coverage; drives how much script is needed.
questions.how_to_answer: Sum of evidence.audio.speech_segments durations / source.duration_s (video_re_speech_segments).
questions.challenge: Voice activity detectors flag sung vocals and dense music; check two segments on an A1 spectrogram.

questions.question: Does the voice sound synthetic (text-to-speech) or recorded human speech?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the pipeline whether a TTS engine can match the delivery.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect A1 spectrograms of 3 sentences: very regular pitch contours, identical prosody on repeated phrases and absent breaths suggest TTS. Method is always inferred.
questions.challenge: Modern TTS can be indistinguishable; confidence above 0.6 needs at least two independent cues.

questions.question: What is the pitch register of the voice (low, mid, high) and the approximate fundamental frequency range?
questions.why_it_matters: Guides voice selection without identifying anyone.
questions.how_to_answer: Read the lowest harmonic band on A1 spectrograms (or use librosa.pyin if installed, marked measured). Report Hz range.
questions.challenge: Answers that infer gender, age or ethnicity are rejected; only pitch and delivery are allowed.

questions.question: What is the speaking rate in words per minute of speech time?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills audio.words_per_minute.
questions.how_to_answer: Read evidence.audio.speech_wpm (video_re_speech_rate); state whether it divides by speech time or by runtime.
questions.challenge: Recompute from caption word count / total speech segment minutes; a mismatch above 10% needs an explanation.

questions.question: How much does speaking rate vary across beats (wpm per beat role)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes per-beat rate targets.
questions.how_to_answer: Words per beat (captions) / speech time per beat.
questions.challenge: Beats with under 10 words give unstable rates; mark them.

questions.question: How long are pauses between sentences and between items (median ms each)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets pause lengths for the TTS plan.
questions.how_to_answer: Gaps between speech segments, split into within-item and at item boundaries.
questions.challenge: Confirm two gaps with A4 silencedetect.

questions.question: What is the dynamic range of the voice (momentary loudness spread during speech)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets compression targets for the narration chain.
questions.how_to_answer: A3 momentary loudness restricted to speech segments; report p10 and p90.
questions.challenge: Music under voice raises the floor; note the music level estimate.

questions.question: How are key words emphasised (louder, slower, higher pitch, pause before)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes emphasis markup rules for TTS (SSML-like or engine-specific).
questions.how_to_answer: Around 4 key numbers or words, compare A6 RMS, local rate and pitch (A1) with neighbouring words.
questions.challenge: Report the measurement per instance.

questions.question: What is the delivery style (conversational, announcer, documentary, energetic hype, calm explainer, whisper)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills delivery for voice selection.
questions.how_to_answer: Combine rate (004), pitch variation (A1), loudness spread (007) and pause pattern (006); method inferred.
questions.challenge: Each style claim must cite at least two measurements.

questions.question: Are breaths audible between phrases or edited out?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes an editing rule for the narration track.
questions.how_to_answer: A1 spectrograms of pauses: broadband soft noise bursts before phrases are breaths.
questions.challenge: Check 4 pauses.

questions.question: How is the voice processed (dry or with room reverb; heavy or light compression; de-essing)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills the voice processing chain.
questions.how_to_answer: A1: reverb tails extend energy after words end; compression shows narrow loudness spread (007); sibilance bands near 5-9 kHz.
questions.challenge: Each processing claim needs its cue.

questions.question: Is the voice bright or warm (where is most energy, above or below about 1 kHz)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills EQ guidance.
questions.how_to_answer: A1 spectrogram energy distribution during speech; compare with A6 RMS after highpass=f=2000 versus lowpass=f=500.
questions.challenge: Report the two filtered RMS values.

questions.question: Is the voice clearly dominant over music during speech (approximate level difference in dB)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets voice-to-music balance.
questions.how_to_answer: A5 mid versus side loudness during speech (stereo only), or A6 RMS during speech versus in speech gaps with music only.
questions.challenge: Side-channel estimates fail when music is near mono; check A7 channels and say which method was used.

questions.question: How soon after a cut does speech start, when a sentence starts at a cut?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets cut-to-voice latency.
questions.how_to_answer: For cuts followed by a speech segment start within 1 s, compute the delay; median.
questions.challenge: Report n.

questions.question: How many distinct voices speak (narrator, characters, quoted speakers)?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides how many voice slots the format needs.
questions.how_to_answer: A1 spectrograms: distinct pitch ranges and timbres; F1 frames for on-screen speakers.
questions.challenge: One narrator changing tone is one voice.

questions.question: Are pitch or character effects applied to voices (sped-up, robotic, telephone filter)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds voice effects.
questions.how_to_answer: A1 for formant shifts and band-limiting.
questions.challenge: Timestamp each effect.

questions.question: What is the noise floor in speech gaps without music (dBFS)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the cleanliness target for narration.
questions.how_to_answer: A6 RMS in gaps where A1 shows no music.
questions.challenge: If music fills every gap, answer not determinable.

questions.question: Do sentences end with falling intonation, rising intonation (upspeak), or flat?
questions.why_it_matters: Guides prosody settings.
questions.how_to_answer: A1: track the lowest harmonic in the last word of 6 sentences.
questions.challenge: Questions naturally rise; exclude them.

questions.question: Is there evidence that speech was time-stretched to fit picture (unnatural rate shifts, smeared consonants, pitch artefacts)?
questions.why_it_matters: A quality rule: this project forbids time-stretching speech to fit.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare local wpm across sentences and inspect A1 for phase smearing on fast passages.
questions.challenge: Natural rate changes are common; require an artefact, not just a rate change.

questions.question: Is each item's narration contained within its beat, or does speech spill over beat boundaries?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a narration-to-beat alignment rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Check whether speech segments cross item boundaries by more than 300 ms.
questions.challenge: Report the share and the crossings.

questions.question: What language is the narration in, and is it consistent?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills narration language for TTS and caption tools.
questions.how_to_answer: From captions or transcription output language tag (evidence.tools or adapter output); confirm by reading two caption cards (analysis only).
questions.challenge: Do not infer nationality or accent origin of the speaker.

questions.question: Which narration parameters should a new video set (voice engine, voice id, wpm range, pause lengths, delivery)?
questions.why_it_matters: Feeds the parameteriser.
questions.how_to_answer: Collect 004, 006, 009 and 012 into parameters; engine and voice are open slots (licensed or local TTS).
questions.challenge: No parameter may reference cloning the source voice.

questions.question: Write the narration budget rule (words per beat = beat_s x wpm / 60 x speech share).
questions.why_it_matters: Lets the script writer hit beat lengths without stretching speech.
questions.how_to_answer: Use 001, 004 and per-beat coverage; test on 3 beats.
questions.challenge: Predict words for 3 observed beats; errors over 20% reject the rule.

questions.question: Are numbers spoken digit by digit, as full words, or abbreviated (for example 'three point two million')?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a text normalisation rule before TTS.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare spoken numbers (A1 timing and captions) with on-screen digits.
questions.challenge: Check 3 numbers.

questions.question: Is the voice centred in the stereo image (mono-compatible)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills voice panning.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare A5 side loudness during speech with mid loudness: near-silent side during speech-only passages means centred.
questions.challenge: Mono files make this trivially true; check A7 channels first.

questions.question: Is the narrator seen on screen (lip-synced presenter) or off-screen (voiceover)?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether a presenter shot is part of the format.
questions.how_to_answer: F2 bursts during speech: visible mouth movement matching speech.
questions.challenge: Do not identify the presenter.

questions.question: Does music with sung vocals overlap the narration?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a mix rule (instrumental under narration).
questions.how_to_answer: A1 during speech: a second harmonic series with sustained notes.
questions.challenge: Give a timestamp.

questions.question: How many seconds before the end does narration stop?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the narration end offset.
questions.how_to_answer: source.duration_s - last speech_segments end_s.
questions.challenge: Recompute.

questions.question: Does narration deliberately stop for music or sound moments (planned silences), and how many?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds planned narration gaps.
questions.how_to_answer: Speech gaps over 1 s where music or sfx rises (A3).
questions.challenge: List each gap.

questions.question: Is the recording tone consistent throughout (same mic, room and level), or patched from sessions?
questions.why_it_matters: A quality rule for TTS or recorded narration (render in one pass or match levels).
questions.how_to_answer: Compare A1 spectral shape and noise floor across the beginning, middle and end.
questions.challenge: Name the segments compared.

questions.question: Which open-source TTS engines could approximate this delivery (for example Kokoro, Piper, Pocket TTS), and which settings matter (rate, voice, pauses)?
questions.why_it_matters: Gives the render binding a TTS hint; always inferred.
questions.how_to_answer: Match measured rate, register and delivery to engines available locally; never propose cloning the source voice.
questions.challenge: Reject any hint that involves voice cloning of the source speaker.
